## S1 Scope, period and currentness

[Foreword, PDF pages 12-16](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=12)
explains the June 2025 cutoff, incorporated amendments, materiality and how
status pages identify affected paragraphs. It expressly says this edition
incorporates only SFFAS 59 land RSI requirements effective for 2022-2025 and
leaves FY2026 disclosure changes for later handbook updates. Do not equate the
compilation's date with a complete determination for FY2026.

The official [Standards & Guidance listing](https://fasab.gov/accounting-standards/)
was read during this task; verification was recorded at
2026-10-25T04:00:21Z. It described this PDF as the current handbook but listed
these issuances as **not included**:

- Technical Bulletin 2025-1, Technical Clarifications: SFFAS 59.
- Staff Implementation Guidance 64.1, Guidance for Implementing SFFAS 64.
- Technical Release 24, Implementation Guidance for Public-Private Partnerships.

It separately listed **pending SFFAS 65: Embedded Leases Practical Expedient**
as informational and pending sponsor/congressional review. This is a dated
listing observation, not verification of the substantive content, effective
dates or later status of those linked documents; they were not independently
retrieved in this task. Retrieve applicable final text and check status at use
time. Do not apply a pending standard as an issued, effective requirement.

The topical/effective-date indexes begin at
[PDF page 2794, Appendix A](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=2794)
and [PDF page 2810, Appendix B](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=2810).
These entry points were located through the outline; they are navigation aids,
not a claim that every indexed topic was inspected.

## S2 GAAP authority and framework exceptions

[SFFAS 34 paragraphs 4-5, PDF page 1200 / chapter page 4](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=1200)
defines applicability and the descending four-category hierarchy: Standards
and Interpretations; Technical Bulletins and specifically applicable cleared
AICPA guidance; Technical Releases; then staff guides and recognized prevalent
federal practice.

[Paragraphs 6-8, PDF page 1201 / chapter page 5](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=1201)
require the highest applicable category, then permissible analogy within
categories A-D before other accounting literature. Concepts are included in
other literature, not the authoritative GAAP categories. The
[SFFAC Preamble, PDF page 17](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=17)
also expressly distinguishes concepts from GAAP.

[Paragraphs 9-11, PDF page 1202 / chapter page 6](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=1202)
address certain entities' continued FASB reporting and rare first-time FASB
use under stated conditions and consultation. Do not erase these qualifications
or assume a government contractor is itself a FASAB reporting entity.

## S3 Cost purpose, full cost and assignment

[SFFAS 4 paragraphs 61-65, PDF page 456 / chapter page 19](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=456)
discusses measurement for different purposes and reconcilable cost measures
traceable to common source data. These paragraphs are managerial cost
accounting concepts, distinct from the five standards identified in the
[SFFAS 4 summary, PDF pages 438-439](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=438).
Do not elevate a conceptual passage solely because it appears in an SFFAS
chapter; the skill's reconciliation workflow is also a local evidence control.
[Paragraphs 67-69, PDF page 457 / chapter page 20](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=457)
describe regular, consistent managerial costing.

[Paragraphs 89-92, PDF pages 463-464 / chapter pages 26-27](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=463)
address full costs of outputs, direct/indirect costs, support services and
unassigned organizational costs. Paragraph 89 distinguishes general-purpose
full-cost reporting from internal/special-purpose studies, for which entity
management judges the appropriate basis.

[Paragraphs 116-128 and the costing-methodology standard, PDF pages 473-475 / chapter pages 36-38](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=473)
prefer economically feasible direct tracing, then cause-and-effect assignment,
then reasonable and consistent allocation. This is a source-based priority,
not approval for a default allocation percentage or duplicated shared costs.

## S4 Inter-entity costs are qualified, not blanket imputation

[Amended SFFAS 4 paragraphs 108-113A, PDF pages 469-472 / chapter pages 32-35](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=469)
must be read with recognition qualifications, not just the broad full-cost
summary. Paragraph 111 distinguishes business-type activities and
non-business-type activities, including exceptions/elections and OMB direction.
Paragraphs 112-113 add materiality, relationship and identifiability criteria.
Paragraph 113A addresses component-entity disclosure.

[SFFAS 4 status, PDF page 438](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=438)
and [SFFAS 55, PDF pages 1880-1882](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=1880)
identify the amendments to those provisions. Applicable implementation
guidance requires its own current-status review. The legacy reference to TR 8
in SFFAS 4 footnote 33B does not restore it:
[TR 19 status and paragraphs 1-3, PDF pages 2674-2676 / chapter pages 1-3](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=2674)
rescinds TR 8 in its entirety, effective upon issuance on January 15, 2019,
because it no longer agrees with amended SFFAS 4. SFFAS 55's status also
identifies the rescission. Do not apply TR 8 as current guidance or claim that
every other implementation topic was inspected.

## S5 Transaction recognition is not spending authority

[SFFAS 1 paragraphs 57-61, PDF page 300 / chapter page 14](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=300)
addresses advances/prepayments paid, their asset reduction as the relevant
conditions occur, received advances as liabilities, non-netting and
intragovernmental presentation. Its progress-payment qualification prevents a
universal inference that all early contract payments are prepayments.

[Paragraphs 74-80, PDF pages 302-303 / chapter pages 16-17](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=302)
addresses payables, title/receipt and work-progress estimates. Missing invoices
do not automatically eliminate accrued amounts. Recognition is fact-specific;
acceptance, constructive receipt and contract performance need examination.

[SFFAS 5 paragraphs 19-22 and footnote 11, PDF page 521 / chapter page 13](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=521)
states liability recognition principles and distinguishes executory contracts
without received goods/services from financial liabilities, even when the
contracts can be budgetary obligations. Financial recognition does not
authorize the obligation or determine procurement legality.

## S6 Assets, software, cloud and materiality

[SFFAS 6 paragraph 13, PDF page 575 / chapter page 9](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=575)
leaves capitalization thresholds to entities' circumstances rather than
establishing a universal Board threshold. This is not the complete PP&E
recognition standard; inspect the relevant asset requirements before use.

[SFFAS 10 paragraphs 15-27, PDF pages 756-758 / chapter pages 7-9](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=756)
covers internal use software, development-stage eligible costs, timing,
conversion, acceptance cutoff, bundles, thresholds, enhancements and
maintenance. It does not capitalize every software-related dollar.

[Amended TR 16 paragraphs 26A-32, PDF pages 2619-2620 / chapter pages 9-10](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=2619)
distinguishes perpetual licenses, license/service components and contractual
software rights in cloud/shared arrangements. Old paragraphs 26-27 are marked
rescinded; amended paragraphs 26A-27A must not be replaced with obsolete text.
[TR 23 status, PDF page 2762 / chapter page 1](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=2762)
identifies the restored/amended guidance and its effective period.

[Foreword materiality, PDF pages 15-16](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=15)
requires entity/fact-specific quantitative and qualitative judgment. No
universal materiality percentage, useful life or capitalization dollar amount
follows from this skill. Subordinate implementation guidance does not override
the applicable standard.

## S7 Budget and accrual reconciliation

[SFFAS 53 paragraphs 1-3, PDF pages 1821-1822 / chapter pages 3-4](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=1821)
addresses component-entity reporting and amends SFFAS 7 paragraphs 80-82 to
reconcile net cost of operations and net outlays, including timing/noncash and
capitalization differences. Paragraph 1 excludes the consolidated financial
report of the U.S. Government as a whole from this information requirement.

[SFFAS 53 status, PDF page 1819](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf#page=1819)
identifies SFFAS 22 as rescinded and the amended standards. The entire SFFAS 7
chapter is not a single authority category: its second part contains concepts.
Use the controlling amended normative paragraphs, not a superseded statement
of financing or a concepts-only passage as a mandatory accounting rule.

## S8 Local adaptations and unverified coverage

The fact-to-criterion brief, permission/evidence controls, qualified-owner
review, model-to-record bridge and Factory daily-rate integration are local
operational adaptations. FASAB does not prescribe the Factory's AI/blended
rates, approve its ROI policy or turn those estimates into journal amounts.

This task did not inspect every handbook chapter, all agency implementation
policies or the separately listed later issuances. Specialized questions need
their own controlling-source research. Do not infer a complete compliance
assessment, audit opinion, approved posting or acquisition/funds authority
from this source map.
